Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) fell today, finishing down 9% amid a sea of red as chip stocks gave back some of Monday's Nvidia-led gains.

The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.4% on Tuesday, while the S&P 500 lost 0.5%.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

AMD stock's Monday rally didn't survive Tuesday

AI-related stocks, especially chip stocks like AMD, jumped Monday after Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) brought back CEO Jensen Huang -- a move many thought wasn't under any serious consideration. That rally faded today, however, as investors tried to decide what, if anything, Huang's return means long term for companies outside of Nvidia.

AMD's sales forecast calls for more growth

AMD's data center revenue nearly doubled in its last quarter, helped by booming sales of server processors and the launch of its latest AI chips. The chipmaker expects overall sales to reach about $17 billion this quarter. Its massive chip deployment with Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT) is due to start in the coming year.

That's all positive, sure, but with a stock trading at 15 times sales -- even after its 36% decline over the last seven weeks -- I would be cautious about buying AMD at the moment. Especially with all of the uncertainty in the market.

title: A scandal like the one haunting Nvidia just reached AMD, its biggest rival
detail:
A scandal like the one haunting Nvidia just reached AMD, its biggest rival
Peace Longe, Celine Provini
Tue, November 24, 2026 at 6:17 PM EST 4 min read
AMD
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Shares of Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) dropped as much as 11% on Nov. 19, 2026. They dropped after a short-selling firm claimed that the chipmaker might have deeper ties to China than it has disclosed to investors.

After the report, CNBC confirmed that AMD closed at $489.19 that day, after dropping about 7.7%. That one afternoon wiped out close to $70 billion of the company's market value, which was above $800 billion before the trading day opened. 

Also read: CoreWeave stuns Wall Street as Nvidia scandal deepens

The short seller claims that sent AMD stock tumbling

Hunterbrook Media published the report on Nov. 19. In it, the short seller claimed that AMD is exposed to Chinese server maker IEIT Systems, a company the U.S. Commerce Department added to its Entity List in March 2025.

And American firms are restricted from selling technology to the names on that list without special approval.

Now Hunterbrook is saying IEIT posted at least six server updates that contain AMD's newer "TurinPI" firmware. AMD first released that specific firmware in July 2026, Wccftech reported.

The report flags AMD's 2025 revenue from China and Hong Kong, which reached $7.75 billion, or 22.4% of total sales. It also highlighted its 2025 Singapore revenue, which came in at 12.4% of the company's fiscal 2025 revenue, according to AMD's 10-K filing with the SEC.

AMD CEO Lisa Su has led the chipmaker's growth into the artificial intelligence market.Austin American-Statesman/Hearst Newspapers / Getty Images
Why this reaches past Wall Street and into regular wallets

AMD designs the chips inside many of our everyday devices, including personal computers, Sony's PlayStation, Microsoft's Xbox, and large facilities like data center servers. The stock also ranks among the largest companies on the Nasdaq 100. 

The Nasdaq 100 shows up inside almost every major retirement fund in the country. So when AMD drops nearly 8% in one session, it reduces — albeit not significantly — the savings of people who might not even pay attention to the market. 

AMD's response and where Lisa Su stands

AMD responded to the report, saying, "The claims misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships," CNBC reported. The company added that it "complies with applicable U.S. export control laws and regulations" and has "rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations."

Hunterbrook itself admitted that its findings do not prove AMD broke any rules, only that the software link deserves a closer look, Yahoo Finance reported.

Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) plunged 8.86% on Tuesday, November 24, closing at $413.27 as renewed selling pressure swept across the semiconductor industry.

Trading volume reached 45.7 million shares, approximately 64% above its three-month daily average of 27.8 million, reflecting heightened investor activity amid the latest sell-off.

How the markets moved today

S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) fell 0.50% to 7,201, while the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) declined 1.48% to 23,734. Among semiconductor peers, Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) closed at $155.38, down 5.86%, and Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) closed at $54.80, down 8.15%, underscoring the pressure across the chipmakers.

What this means for investors

AMD's latest sell-off highlights growing uncertainty surrounding the financial implications of large-scale AI partnerships. Adding to these concerns, the company recently filed a registration covering approximately 337 million shares for potential resale, raising questions about future shareholder dilution. Although the filing does not represent an immediate sale of shares, investors should consider how these arrangements could affect existing shareholders and prices.

Despite the recent volatility, AMD's underlying business continues to demonstrate strong growth. The company recently reported record quarterly revenue and raised its outlook, supported by demand for its data center processors and AI accelerators.

Looking ahead, AMD's ability to translate growing AI demand into sustained profitability will be critical. While the recent decline could present an attractive entry point, the combination of potential dilution, competitive pressures, and elevated semiconductor valuations warrants caution.

title: Dow Brushes Off Tech Rout, Tariff Worries to Add 423 Points: Stock Market Today

AMD

Credit: Getty Images

Stocks opened lower Tuesday as the technology rout resumed and sharp losses for several mega-cap artificial intelligence (AI) stocks, including Nvidia (NVDA, -5.9%) and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD, -8.9%), weighed on the broader market.

At the close, the Nasdaq Composite was down 1.5% at 23,733 and the S&P 500 was 0.5% lower at 7,201. But the price-weighted Dow Jones Industrial Average found its way into positive territory by lunchtime, and finished the day up 0.9% at 50,018.

"A renewal of AI safety worries and tariff concerns" had tech stocks giving back a portion of Monday's big gains, says José Torres, senior economist at Interactive Brokers. "Anecdotal evidence suggests that Anthropic and OpenAI employees believe some of the newest technologies are too potent for humanity, heightening angst about a slowdown in the adoption, integration and capital expenditures that would support the buildout of the most advanced models."

Anthropic (ANT) slid 6.5% today, closing below its $83 initial public offering (IPO) price for the first time since it began trading last Thursday.

Track all markets on TradingView

Torres also points to reports that the Trump administration is preparing to raise tariffs on China, the European Union and several other trading partners, "which is further hurting the corporate earnings outlook, as 2027 profit growth projections have been trimmed in the past few weeks."

Looking for more timely stock market news to help gauge the health of your portfolio? Sign up for Closing Bell, our free newsletter that's delivered straight to your inbox at the close of each trading day.

Retail stocks rise ahead of Black Friday

On the positive side of the ledger, retailers were some of the biggest gainers ahead of the annual Black Friday shopping event. Abercrombie & Fitch (ANF) jumped 19.7% after the specialty clothing retailer reported better-than-expected fiscal third-quarter results and raised its full-year forecast.

Dick's Sporting Goods (DKS) soared 14.6% after its own beat-and-raise quarter. The sporting goods retailer disclosed a surprise return to same-store-sales growth in its Foot Locker segment, "despite a continued challenging athletic footwear marketplace," said Executive Chairman Ed Stack.

This gave a halo lift to Nike (NKE), which jumped 5.9%, making it the best Dow Jones stock on Tuesday. The athletic apparel and footwear maker will report its fiscal 2027 second-quarter results after the close on Thursday, December 17.
